correctness.rationale: The classical square-free criterion makes the exceptional set exactly \(2m\) with \(m\) square-free and supported on primes congruent to \(1\pmod4\). Its Dirichlet series factors as \(\zeta(s)^{1/2}G(s)\) with \(G\) regular at \(1\); Landau–Selberg–Delange gives the \(x/\sqrt{\log x}\) term. The Euler-product constant simplifies to \(2K_{\mathrm{LR}}/\pi^2\) after the exact rescaling by \(2\). The standard square-free count then yields the stated secondary term. The packaged checker independently confirms the structural criterion through \(10^6\) and numerically corroborates the constant.

value.rationale: The square-free stratum is the classical clean test case for arithmetic numbers. The result turns its qualitative criterion into a sharp first correction to the square-free density, identifies the exact decay rate of the exceptional proportion, and links the coefficient to the classical Landau–Ramanujan constant. This is a natural structural asymptotic rather than an arbitrary finite slice or table recomputation.
